chunks: Aban, from Zurara bin A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:
I asked about the man who marries the slave girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he is compelled to do so.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a free man to marry a slave girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that while a free man marrying a slave girl is generally permissible, it is not the preferred norm unless there is a state of necessity (idtirar), such as the inability to afford a free wife. This ruling reflects the practical socio-legal context of early Islamic society, where marriage to slave girls was regulated to ensure lineage and rights, distinguishing it from the ideal of marrying free women. The condition of 'compulsion' highlights the juristic principle of easing restrictions in cases of genuine need rather than mere preference.

en.hubeali:
Aban, from Zurara Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked about the man who marries the slave girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except if he is desperate to that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Aban has narrated from Zurarah ibn ‘A‘yan who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the marriage of a slave-girl. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, unless it is an emergency.’”
